Build your own catering: choose the menu, the quality and the price

November 11, 2026 · By the Tailwinds team

Catering used to be one of five fixed levels. You can now build your own service, cabin by cabin, and put it on whichever routes you like. It is under Operations, in a new Service Plans section, in new and existing saves. The five classic levels are still there and work exactly as before.

  • A menu of ten items. Water, soft drinks, beer and wine, spirits, champagne, a snack, a cold meal, a hot meal, extra courses, and fine dining in business and first. Switch each one on or off for each cabin.
  • Three quality tiers. Meals, snacks, wine and champagne come as Basic, Standard or Premium. Basic costs 60% of Standard and passengers value it at 70%. Premium costs 150% and is valued at 125%.
  • Free or sold, at your price. A free item goes to everyone and you pay for everyone. A sold item goes only to the passengers who buy it, at the price you type. Charge more and fewer buy. The game does not suggest a price: it shows what the item costs you and what your price does.
  • Quality follows the menu. Free food counts in full. Sold food counts for less, and less again the more you charge. Serve each cabin what it expects and you match the old Full Service; go beyond it, or go Premium, and you can beat it. This feeds route quality and your reputation the same way catering always has.
  • Every choice is costed on screen. For each item the editor shows the cost per passenger, how many buy, the sales and the net, and a bar for the quality it adds. A mark on the bar shows what the item would add if it were free. Each cabin and the whole plan get a total and a bar of their own.
  • Short and long flights want different menus. Under 1,000 km a meal counts for half what it does on long haul, and drinks and a snack count for more. From 4,000 km the meal is most of what passengers judge. Catering costs still rise with distance.
  • Apply in bulk or route by route. Apply to routes lists your network filtered by flight length, region or hub, with the change in catering money and quality for each route. Your plans also appear in every catering picker and in the bulk bar on the Routes page, and any plan can be the default for new routes. Edit a plan and every route on it follows the next week.
  • Start from a classic level. Customise on any classic level opens a copy you can edit, filled in with the matching items. The copy lands close to the original, not exactly on it.
  • Caterers. A catering contract does not cap a plan by level. The caterer leaves out what its kitchen cannot make at the airports it cooks for, you pay only for what is served, and the route screen names what is missing.
